questions.question: Describe the social structure of ancient Egypt from top to bottom.
questions.expected_answer: At the top was the pharaoh, believed to be a god on Earth. Below were the vizier, nobles and priests, then scribes and soldiers, then craftspeople and traders, then the large group of farmers, and at the bottom, servants and enslaved people. It was shaped like a pyramid, with few people at the top and many at the bottom.

questions.question: Explain the role of the pharaoh.
questions.expected_answer: The pharaoh was the king and was believed to be a god on Earth, the link between the gods and the people. He owned all the land, made the laws, led the army, collected taxes and was the chief priest, keeping order and pleasing the gods so the Nile would flood and harvests would be good.

questions.question: Describe the rights and roles of women in ancient Egypt.
questions.expected_answer: Egyptian women had more rights than in many ancient societies. They could own and inherit property, buy and sell, run businesses, make contracts and go to court. Most ran the home and raised children, but some were weavers, bakers, musicians, priestesses or officials, and Hatshepsut ruled as pharaoh. The most powerful positions were still mostly held by men.
